pl985706528.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl985706528.description: A Kushite site located on Argo Island in Nubia, the location of a large Amun temple.

pl805649.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl805649.description: The one-time capital of the ancient Kerma culture in Nubia.

pl97711900.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl97711900.description: The pyramid tombs of the kings of the Kushite kingdom.

pl579500116.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl579500116.description: Large temple dedicated to the Amun located at the base of Jebel Barkal. Designated temple B500, the structure was likely constructed by the Napatan king Piankhi in the 8th century BCE.

pl805647.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl805647.description: Known today as Kawa, ruins of this ancient Egyptian and Kushite settlement are located on the east bank of the Nile river, seven kilometers south of the modern Nile bridge at Dongola in Sudan.

pl763458797.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl763458797.description: The Yeha Temple is alleged to be among the oldest known extant structures in Ethiopia. It is executed in the Sabaean style and may date to the seventh century BCE.

pl805623.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl805623.description: El-Kurru is the site of a necropolis used by Nubian royalty. Many of the royal tombs date to the Kushite period.

pl43832477.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl43832477.description: The Pre-Aksumite settlement of Sembel, located near Asmara in Ethiopia, dates ca. 800 BCE.

cur-meroe.dateNote: Dated c. 800 BCE, when Meroë first appears as a town of the Kingdom of Kush (Wikipedia). The royal burials moved here from Napata about 300 BCE.

pl805632.description: A Meroitic temple complex in modern Sudan, located 180 km northeast of Khartoum, 20 km north of Naqa and approximately 25 km south-east of the Nile. The complex dates to the early Meroitic period (third century B.C.). In 2011 the site was enrolled as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

pl862402774.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl862402774.description: The archaeological site of Keskese is located approximately 8 km north of Matara. It is the site of numerous stelai dating ca. 500 BCE.

pl805634.description: Napata was a Nubian city-state located on the west bank of the Nile River and founded in the fifteenth century B.C.

pl403627899.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403627899.description: Matara, in Eritrea, is an archaeological site located along the coast road to Adulis and dating to pre-Aksumite or early Aksumite times. It is possibly to be identified as the Koloe mentioned in a Roman imperial source.

pl698596572.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl698596572.description: A pre-Aksumite and Aksumite settlement located in what is now southern Eritrea, possibly to be identified as the Koloe mentioned in a Roman imperial source. Qohaito has been submitted by Eritrea for consideration as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

pl204558111.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl204558111.description: The Temple of Apedemak, also known as the Lion Temple, is located to the west of the temple of Amun.

pl29407544.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl29407544.description: Hamadab is an important archaeological site of the middle Nile River valley. It is the site of a ruined Kushite city located in what is now Sudan. The settlement was established by the third century BCE and remained active until the fourth century CE.

pl39271.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl39271.description: An ancient market settlement and port on the west coast of the Red Sea near modern Zula in Eritrea.

pl39409.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl39409.description: Ptolemais Theron was an ancient marketplace on the western coast of the Red Sea. Its precise location on the Sudanese Red Sea coast is now unknown, but many scholars view modern Aqiq (Hillat `Agig) as the most likely alternative.

pl128897485.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl128897485.description: Temple structure located south of the main Amun Temple complex at Naga, constructed during the reign of King Nebmaatre Amanakhareqerema (1st century CE).

pl794683793.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl794683793.description: An expansive area of funereal monuments at Aksum in Ethiopia, built between the third and fourth centuries A.D.

pl865674318.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl865674318.description: The late antique capital of the Nubian state of Makuria, Dongola remained an important center of trade through the medieval period.

q323363.dateNote: Wikidata gives only the 6th century for his birth; 501 is only a placeholder. He died about 570.

q449639.dateNote: Alodia was a kingdom, not one place, so the pin is only rough; its capital was Soba, near Khartoum. It is first recorded in the 6th century.

pl224949836.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl224949836.description: The Southeastern Cluster of rock-cut churches at Lalibela.

q7971367.dateNote: The year shown, 1200, stands for the late 12th or early 13th century, in the reign of King Lalibela. Only the rough time is known.

q471332.placeNote: Born at Roha, by the account of his life (the Gadla Lalibela); the town was later renamed Lalibela after him. A few sources say Adefa or Bugna, nearby.

q558437.placeNote: The pin is Debre Damo, where he died in 1540; where he was born is not well recorded.

q326449.placeNote: Where he was born is disputed: Ethiopia or Eritrea by older accounts, or Logone-Birni (Cameroon) by recent research. The pin is in Ethiopia.

pl793286641.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl793286641.description: Sabu-Jaddi is the site of multi-period Nubian rock art and is located along the Nile River downstream of the third cataract region on the east bank of the Nile. These rock drawings are found on sandstone cliffs between the Sudanese villages of Sabu and Jaddi.

pl403627900.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl403627900.description: Lalibela is an ancient site in in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia known especially for its 11 rock-cut churches.

q262589.placeNote: Where he was born is not recorded; the pin is just the middle of Qwara.

q1963.dateNote: Wikipedia: "founded in 1821 by Muhammad Ali Pasha, north of the ancient city of Soba"

q309475.dateNote: 1821 is when the Egyptian army took El-Obeid. The town was already the main town of Kordofan before that, but when it began is not known.

pl902590390.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl902590390.description: Jebel Shaqadud (Sudan) is an archaeological site located 115 km northeast of Khartoum. It preserves at least 7 meters of in situ stratified deposits that date from ca. 8,200 to 4,000 cal BP.

q895930.placeNote: Pinned at the centre of Sudan. Wikidata records the country where this happened but not a place within it, so the marker shows the country, not the spot.

cur-fossil-gona.dateNote: In 1992–94 Sileshi Semaw's team dug sharp stone flakes and cores out of old river beds at Gona, in the Afar region of Ethiopia. Reported in 1997, they are about 2.6 million years old: for years the oldest stone tools known. Wikidata pins the site at a rounded point.
cur-fossil-gona.summary: Where 2.6-million-year-old stone tools, long the oldest known, were found in Ethiopia.

pl253102124.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl253102124.description: Archaeological investigation at the site of Beta Samati, located between Aksum and the Red Sea, has revealed remains of a significant Aksumite administrative center. The archaeological site is located in the vicinity of Yeha, Ethiopia.

pl750315751.source: Pleiades (pleiades.stoa.org), Institute for the Study of the Ancient World, CC-BY 3.0
pl750315751.description: Jebel Moya is an archaeological site located in the southern part of the Gezira Plain in Sudan. The 25-acre site was the locus of the largest-known pastoralist necropolis in Africa, with more than 3,000 burials dating between 5000 BCE and 500 CE. Sir Henry Wellcome first excavated the site from 1911 to 1914.
